newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tin steadies after post-budget fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian tin steadies after post-budget fall.

text.p: Tin prices steadied on the Indian market after recent sharp falls in reaction to a proposed cut in import duties.
Other base metals were quiet and price movements small, traders said.
Tin was steady at 31,500 rupees per quintal on fresh physical enquiries and limited offerings. Tin fell 800 rupees last week and 2,800 rupees per quintal during the last fortnight.
A proposal in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget presented on February 28 to lower the import duty on tin to 20 percent from 30 percent triggered heavy unloading by stockists.
Zinc fell 50 rupees to 7,450 rupees per quintal as weak world prices prompted profit-taking and demand resistance capped gains.

Copper was quiet at 13,350 rupees so was aluminium at 7,400 rupees and lead at 4,525 rupees per quintal amid nominal trading but sentiment was subdued as physical enquiries were low and traders were complaining strigent monetary conditions.
Nickel was steady at the improved level of 37,300 rupees per quintal after gaining 200 rupees on Saturday.
